Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Bangladesh's reply with the bat. Suryakumar Yadav has his men in a huddle near the ropes. Tanzid Hasan and Saif Hassan are the two openers for Bangladesh. Hardik Pandya will start with the new ball for India. Hardik to Saif. A slip in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, 168 feels just about par, and the way Bangladesh bowled in the last two overs could prove decisive by the end of the night. They chased 169 against Sri Lanka to kickstart their Super Four campaign, and that is the target they are facing tonight as well but they are without the experience of Litton Das in this game. What was noticeable was that as the ball got older, it became harder to find the big shots compared to the Powerplay with the hard new ball. The Tigers will be looking to get a strong start in the chase, while India will be on the lookout for early wickets, which have eluded them so far. Back in a bit for the second essay.

Just when it looked ominous for Bangladesh, Rishad Hossain’s double strike provided the breakthrough and slowed India’s charge. He then made his presence felt in the field as well, playing a key role in the run-out of Abhishek Sharma, which really put the brakes on the scoring. From there, Bangladesh made further inroads and kept the scoring in check. Hardik Pandya helped India inch close to the 170-mark, but thanks to the efforts of Mohammad Saifuddin and Mustafizur Rahman at the death, India were restricted to 168, with only 13 runs coming off the final two overs.

Excellent final over from Mohammad Saifuddin, and that caps off a terrific effort from Bangladesh to pull things back. India’s innings really was a tale of two halves. The first 10 overs - 96/2, while the next 10 overs - 72/4. After opting to bowl first, Bangladesh showed promise in the opening couple of overs, but it all unravelled once Abhishek Sharma found his rhythm. The left-hander launched a blistering assault that left the Tigers under serious pressure, as India raced to 72 without loss in the Powerplay.

OUT! GONE! CAUGHT! This is a very positive finish for Bangladesh! On a fullish length, at 128.7 kph, angling on the off stump line, Hardik Pandya attempts to sail it over long off, but neither does he get the distance nor the height for doing so. Ends up sailing it straight into the hands of the fielder stationed at long off. Tanzid Hasan takes a simple catch over his head. Just 4 runs off the final over. INDIA FINISH WITH 168/6 ON THE BOARD!

OUT! ABHISHEK SHARMA IS RUN OUT! Rishad Hossain can do no wrong tonight. This is pushed across the right-hander, on a back of a length. Suryakumar hangs back and steers it with an open bat face towards backward point. Rishad dives to his left but Abhishek sets off for the run and does not wait for the ball to get past the fielder. Hossain cuts it off with a dive to his left but sticks out his right hand to grab the ball. Gets rid of the ball immediately as he gets up on his feet and throws it on the bounce towards the bowling end. Mustafizur Rahman is quick to turn around and get up to the stumps at the bowling end. The throw is at a good height and near the stumps. Fizz collects and disturbs the stumps. The third umpire is called in. Rahman goes at it with both hands but the ball nestles in his left hand. He brings both hands close to the stumps and breaks the stumps with the left hand, the hand he had the ball in before the right hand makes contact with the stumps. Abhishek is well short despite the dive. Abhishek Sharma looks dejected as he walks back for a superb 75 off just 37 deliveries. India are 112/3 down now.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! Bangladesh have done well to pull things back after India’s onslaught in the Powerplay. In the first six overs, Bangladesh conceded 72 without any wickets, but the next four brought two wickets for them while conceding just 24 runs. The Bangla Tigers will be eager to remove Abhishek Sharma quickly after the break and expose another new batter to keep the scoring in check. Tonight's surface here in Dubai has been one of the better batting tracks of the competition, and with the platform already set, India will be disappointed if they do not push past 200 from this position.

Commentary.Commentary: Outside off, on a length. Abhishek Sharma stands tall and punches it hard to the right of the diving cover fielder for a couple of runs as deep point mops it up.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Rishad Hossain to Abhishek Sharma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Onto the pads, Dube flicks that behind square on the leg side for a single and gets off the mark!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Rishad Hossain to Shivam Dube, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A promotion for Shivam Dube as he walks in at number 3. A slip in place for the new batter.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND TAKEN! Rishad Hossain provides the first breakthrough for Bangladesh and breaks the dangerous-looking opening stand of India! Hossain serves it up, tosses it around off on a fuller length. Shubman Gill accepts the invite and tries to smash it over long off, but does not get his bat underneath the ball properly. Hence, the bat gets twisted at the point of contact and the ball is sliced towards long off. Tanzim Hasan Sakib stationed in the deep, moves a bit to his right, judges the trajectory well and takes a good catch at the edge of the ropes. Shubman Gill departs for 29 (19) and India are 77/1.
Commentary.Howout: c Tanzim Hasan Sakib b Rishad Hossain
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Rishad Hossain to Shubman Gill, OUT! c Tanzim Hasan Sakib b Rishad Hossain.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Sprayed down leg, full in length. Shubman Gill misses to sweep. Wide called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Rishad Hossain to Shubman Gill, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Excellent placement! Rishad Hossain starts his spell with a juicy half-volley, wide on off. Shubman Gill climbs on it and carves it away to the deep cover region. Saif Hassan from deep point runs to his right and puts in a dive, but does not manage to make the stop as the ball goes under the body.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Rishad Hossain to Shubman Gill, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Make that four boundaries in the over! Mohammad Saifuddin lands it around middle, on a good length. Abhishek Sharma again dances down the track and smashes it over the cover-point region for a boundary. This is India's highest Powerplay score in this Asia Cup. They are 72/0.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Mohammad Saifuddin to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! Shortens the length, on the leg stump line. Abhishek Sharma jumps down the track, stays leg side, and cuts it over backward point for another boundary. Third boundary off this over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Mohammad Saifuddin to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Clean hitting! Back of a length, outside off, angling away. Abhishek Sharma throws his hands at it and thrashes that over cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Mohammad Saifuddin to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On the stumps, Abhishek stays leg side and smashes it straight back to the bowler. The ball deflects off his fingers and rattles the stumps at the other end. Gill, however, has his bat grounded.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Mohammad Saifuddin to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! PUNISHED! Saifuddin tries the yorker, on middle, but Sharma charges down the track and converts that into a full toss. Swings cleanly and manages to find the fence at deep cover. The umpire checks whether the ball has sailed all the way, but the replay shows that it has just bounced a few yards inside the ropes. So, four it is!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Mohammad Saifuddin to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Starts from over the stumps and lands on a good length, just around off. Shubman Gill hangs back and jabs it down to long on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Mohammad Saifuddin to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: 38 runs in the last two overs for India. Mohammad Saifuddin is into the attack. He replaces Nasum Ahmed.

SIX! Flayed away! 50 up for India! This is on a shortish length, outside off. Abhishek stays leg side of the ball and he gets the width to free his arms. Carves it over backward point and clears the fence for another six. An expensive start to the night for Mustafizur Rahman. 17 runs off his first over. 10 runs off the first 2 overs of the game and the next 3 have gone for 45.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Mustafizur Rahman to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Mustafizur rolls his fingers over the ball and bowls it on a good length, on middle and leg. Gill checks his drive and it is chipped uppishly but of the bowler's reach and well in front of mid on. A single taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Mustafizur Rahman to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Not in control but Abhishek gets away with it! Fizz goes into the surface and does not offer much pace, over middle. Sharma swivels for the pull but the ball climbs onto him. Gets it high on the bat but it evades the backtracking mid-wicket fielder. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Mustafizur Rahman to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mustafizur takes pace off and bowls it at 120.4 kph, on a good length, outside off. Abhishek Sharma hangs back to thump it down the ground with a flat bat. Does not quite get hold of it but manages to clear the mid off fielder and collects a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Mustafizur Rahman to Abhishek Sharma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! High and handsome! Not a bad ball by any means by Mustafizur Rahman. On a good length, on middle. Abhishek trusts the bounce of the surface and with a clean extension of the arms, he tonks it over long on for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Mustafizur Rahman to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Angled away, on a length, Gill knocks it in front of mid off and takes a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Mustafizur Rahman to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mustafizur Rahman is brought into the attack now. He replaces Tanzim Hasan Sakib.

SIX! Belted! Nasum fires in a full ball, right in the hitting arc, on middle and leg. Abhishek gets the front leg out of the way and pumps it way over the long on fielder for a six. 21 runs off the over and India are off to a fine start.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Nasum Ahmed to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Fractionally short, around off. Shubman presses back and cuts it between backward point and cover-point. The ball plugs in the outfield as Tawhid Hridoy gives it a chase and flicks the ball behind his body towards the fielder backing up. A good tag team effort. There is a check for a short run but Abhishek Sharma is fine at both ends. Gill adds three more runs to his tally.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Nasum Ahmed to Shubman Gill, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: At 92.9 kph, flatter and shorter, on middle. Abhishek Sharma taps it down the deck where Nasum dives to his left but cannot prevent the ball from going past him. The ball rolls down to long on and the batters cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Nasum Ahmed to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drifting onto the pads, on a length, Gill turns it through square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Nasum Ahmed to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Shubman Gill takes the aerial route this time! Attacking the stumps and the length is pulled back by Nasum. Gill gives the bowler the charge again but does not quite get to the pitch of the ball. Still goes through with the shot and clubs it over deep mid-wicket for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Nasum Ahmed to Shubman Gill, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Excellent use of the feet! Angled in by Nasum from around the wicket, on middle and leg. Shubman skips down the track and gets to the pitch of the ball. Firms the drive all along the ground to the left of mid on for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Nasum Ahmed to Shubman Gill, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Pace taken off by Tanzim, on a good length, on middle. Shubman waits back and wrists it between mid-wicket and mid on. The ball slows down in front of the boundary cushions and it is hauled in by the mid on fielder after a chase. Three runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Shubman Gill, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Sprayed down leg, on a back of a length. Gill swings to help it away but fails to lay any bat on it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Shubman Gill, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Tanzim goes into the surface, over off. Gill swings across for the pull and gets more height than distance on it. Hits it away from the man at deep backward square leg to his left. Shamim Hossain is quick to get around and pushes the ball away from the fence. Saves two runs for his side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Shubman Gill, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Hurls it on a good length, on the off pole. Gill drives it on the up and mistimes it in front of cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: PUT DOWN BY JAKER ALI! A tough chance, but Jaker gave his best. Slams the deck really hard, does Sakib, on top of off and gets the ball to nibble away. Abhishek Sharma hangs the bat away from the body, and gets a thick outside edge. The ball shoots flat and low to the left of Jaker Ali, who flings himself to catch, but the ball deflects off the gloves and runs behind to deep third. A single taken. But this has been a fantastic start with the new ball from Sakib. He hasn't bowled one loose ball to offer any chance to the batter.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! Going across the left-hander, on a good length. Abhishek Sharma again is stationary inside the crease, but tries to whack that over cover, and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Smart bowling! Sakib spots Sharma stepping down the track and bangs it hard on the bodyline of the batter, cramping the left-hander for space. Abhishek is rushed and gets an inside edge onto the front pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sliding on with the arm, on a length, on the pads. Shubman Gill gets forward for the block but the ball sneaks past the bat to rap him on the front pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Nasum Ahmed to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Almost chipped it back! Nasum slows it down and the ball seems to stop on the batter, on a length, on off. Sharma looks to push it down the ground and is early into the shot. Chips it towards the bowler and Ahmed leaps to his right but the ball evades him and goes over his head. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Nasum Ahmed to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Not where Abhishek Sharma intended but he has his first boundary! Speared in by Nasum, on off, on a length. Abhishek stays leg side of the ball and swings to go big on the off side. Gets a thickish outside edge that sails over short third for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Nasum Ahmed to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Floated up, fuller and on off. Shubman Gill lunges and eases it to long off for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Nasum Ahmed to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Low full toss, on off. Abhishek Sharma looks to smash it through the off side but toe-ends the drive wide of mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Nasum Ahmed to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A big swing and a miss! A bit of air given by Nasum, on a nagging length, around off. Sharma clears the front leg and swings to go down the ground but the ball keeps straight and zips past the outside edge. A good take by Jaker Ali and he is quick enough to whip the bails off but Sharma has his back leg grounded inside the crease.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Nasum Ahmed to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Spin from the other end. Nasum Ahmed has been introduced into the attack.
A good tone-setter over from Tanzim Hasan Sakib! In the channel on off, curving away from the right-hander, on a good length. Gill has a feel for the ball and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bangs it on a shortish length, on off. Shubman Gill backs away and looks to flay at it on the off side. Gets an inside edge that rolls away to short fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Uppish but safe! On a good length, moving away in the air, Shubman gets forward but tentatively jabs at the ball. Hits it uppishly but it goes through the gap between backward point and cover-point. Gill gets off the mark with a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Shubman Gill, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Tanzim drags the length back and hits the deck hard, over off. Shubman rises with the bounce and stabs it down the deck with a straight bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! A bit of away shape, on a good length, outside off. Gill throws his hands at it but the ball skids through and goes under the blade.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Abhishek Sharma and India are underway! Tanzim charges in from over the wicket and bashes the hard length, on top of off. Sharma gets on his toes and glides it down with an open bat face to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with all the pre-match rituals. The anthems are sung, and we are all set for this crucial Super 4 fixture to get underway here at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. The umpires are already out and take their spots. The players of Bangladesh spread out of the huddle and scatter all around the field. And out walks the opening pair for India - Abhishek Sharma and Shubman Gill. Jaker Ali, the stand-in captain for Bangladesh in this clash, has taken the gloves. And it will be Tanzim Hasan Sakib to bowl the first over of the match. Abhishek to face. The countdown is done, and 'Let's Play' says the umpire. Here we go...

Just a few minutes to go for the first ball. But before that, both sets of players walk out, followed by the match officials, and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's first, followed by the Indian national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Simon Doull and Ravi Shastri are pitchside with their thoughts. Simon highlights that five out of seven games have been won by the team chasing. Ravi Shastri joins and points out that there is some grass, to which Doull mentions the ground staff being happy with the moisture content in the pitch. Ravi then points out that the reason the seamers have matched the spinners is because the ball has swung, and the bowlers have taken pace off to achieve success. Doull ends by stressing that putting good runs on the board is crucial.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Saif Hassan, Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon (In for Litton Das), Tawhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali (C/WK), Shamim Hossain, Rishad Hossain (In for Mahedi Hasan), Nasum Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Tanzim Hasan Sakib (In for Taskin Ahmed), Mohammad Saifuddin (In for Shoriful Islam).

India (Unchanged Playing XI) - Abhishek Sharma, Shubman Gill, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Tilak Varma, Sanju Samson (WK), Hardik Pandya, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Varun Chakaravarthy, Jasprit Bumrah.

The captain of India, Suryakumar Yadav says that he is happy to bat first. Shares that they have played on this track before and it got slower in the 2nd innings, which is why they wanted to bat first. Believes that it is all about continuing to do the good things and the result will take care of itself. When asked about the dropped catches in the last outing, he replies that it is part of the game and the boys have practised hard since that game. Informs that they are unchanged for this game.

The stand-in captain of Bangladesh, Jaker Ali, first informs that Litton Das misses out in this vital game due to an injury he suffered during practice. Adds they are really excited to play against the best team in the world. Mentions as a team, they are doing well and playing according to their strengths. Further tells that the surface looks good to bat and they will try to restrict them. Informs that they are going with four changes in the side.
TOSS - Jaker Ali has walked out for the coin flip instead of Litton Das. Jaker calls it correctly and Bangladesh have elected to BOWL first.

Playing on back-to-back days in these energy-sapping conditions is tough, but Bangladesh will have to rise to the challenge. They have beaten India only once in this format in 17 meetings and will have to defy the odds. India’s middle order has looked scratchy, and Bangladesh will be keen to exploit that and target early wickets. Dubai has generally been a chasing venue, but chasing has not been as straightforward as it once was. That said, 5 of the 7 games in this Asia Cup here have been won by the side batting second. Stick around for the toss and team news.

Bangladesh, meanwhile, come into this clash on the back of a morale-boosting win over Sri Lanka. It may not have been an upset in the strictest sense, but considering Sri Lanka entered that contest as favourites, especially after winning the group-stage meeting, it was a statement performance. Litton Das and his men will want to keep the equation simple. Win against India and then repeat the dose against Pakistan, and they will be through. However, a defeat tonight would leave them facing a straight shootout against Pakistan tomorrow for a spot in the final.

Pakistan’s win over Sri Lanka last evening has left the islanders walking a tightrope. An Indian win tonight will secure their place in the final while also knocking Sri Lanka out of the race. The Men in Blue began their campaign with a couple of near-perfect games but have since struggled to produce equally polished performances, though they continue to find ways to get over the line. More than anything, they will want to improve their fielding standards after multiple dropped catches in the previous game against Pakistan.

Hello and a warm welcome, everyone. Tonight, we dive into the second half of the Super Four stage as India take on Bangladesh at the Dubai International Stadium. No team has secured a place in the final yet, and no one is out of contention either, but that could change by the end of the night.
... MATCH DAY ...

The Super Four stage of the 2025 Asia Cup moves into game number four, where India face Bangladesh at the Dubai International Stadium. Both teams come into this clash with a win in their opening Super Four fixture and will now be aiming to move a step closer to sealing a spot in the final with another victory. India remain the only unbeaten side in the tournament, having won all four of their games so far. Their Super Four opener saw them get the better of arch-rivals Pakistan. It was not a perfect game as several catches went down and the bowling unit looked below its usual high standards. Jasprit Bumrah, typically reliable, was unusually expensive. However, India found a saviour in Shivam Dube, who stepped up with the ball to pull things back after Pakistan had made a strong start in the first 10 overs. On one of the better batting surfaces in Dubai this Asia Cup, Dube’s spell was one of the biggest positives for the Men in Blue to take away. With the bat, Abhishek Sharma and Shubman Gill broke the back of the chase with a 105-run opening stand, with the former going on to score 74. Abhishek’s breezy starts have ensured that the middle order has not had much to do and, as a result, has not really been tested under pressure. Sanju Samson, in particular, is yet to shrug off the cobwebs and will be eager for another opportunity to spend time in the middle and gain some confidence. On the other hand, Bangladesh will be riding high on confidence after their win over Sri Lanka to kickstart their Super Four campaign. The victory was particularly significant given that they had lost to the same opposition earlier in the group stage, and in a convincing fashion. Mustafizur Rahman showed his class at the death, restricting Sri Lanka to a manageable total. Saif Hassan and Tawhid Hridoy then laid the foundation for the chase, although some ordinary batting while closing in on the finish line left room for improvement. Coming into the tournament, inconsistency at the top had been an issue for the Bangla Tigers. That concern has eased somewhat with Saif and Tawhid among the runs, though Tanzid Hasan and captain Litton Das will need to step up against a strong Indian side. The balance of the XI also looked far better after they went in with Shoriful Islam and Mahedi Hasan, having previously opted for just four frontline bowlers against Afghanistan. However, Shoriful endured a tough outing and will have an important role to play with the new ball, especially with his left-arm angle. The last time Bangladesh defeated India in T20Is was back in 2019, a reminder of the challenge they face against a side that has largely dominated this contest in recent years. Can they click as a unit and spring a surprise this time around? We shall find out.
